Jacob Riis, How the Other Half Lives.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/jacob-riis/how-the-other-half-lives

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Jacob Riis, the author, died 1914 (Wikidata Q379211, P570 = 1914-05-26).

First publication of the text used: 1890 (SE colophon: 'How the Other Half Lives was published in 1890 by Jacob Riis.'). The Wikipedia article says the book was published in January 1890, after a magazine article in Scribner's Magazine, by C. Scribner's Sons.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1890, before 1931, so the US rule settles its origin too. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 1985.
- Country of origin (United States): the US rule settles the origin, whatever the death year (1914), because the first publication was in the United States before 1931.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
